sentences.text: Sibirotitan astrosacralis is the sole species within the genus Sibirotitan, representing a somphospondyl sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Russia.
This dinosaur is distinguished by a high hyposphene ridge on its back bones and by possessing only five sacral vertebrae rather than the typical six found in related somphospondyls.
Estimates suggest the animal weighed approximately 20 tonnes, a mass comparable to that of the Apatosaurus.
The species name astrosacralis describes the star-like arrangement of the sacral ribs when viewed from above.
Definitive sauropod remains were uncovered during expeditions in 1994 and 1995 at the Shestakovo 1 locality in the Ilek Formation near Shestakovo Village in West Siberia.
The genus was formally named by Averianov and colleagues in 2018, combining the location Siberia with the Greek word for 'titan'.
In 2017, researchers named the specimens that could be safely referred to a single taxon S. astrosacralis, making it the second species named in the nation after Tengrisaurus.
A specific dorsal vertebra, cataloged as PM TGU 120/10-Sh1-22, was chosen as the holotype for the species.
Researchers noted that teeth from the site suggested a possible identity as a brachiosaurid, while a tail bone from a nearby site indicated a titanosaurian.
Many scattered fragments are believed to belong to one individual, implying that large remains found in the 1960s might be from the same skeleton as those discovered as recently as 2011.
A single neck bone centrum was reported as belonging to a different juvenile individual, while the rest of the material belongs to an adult animal.
Phylogenetic analysis classifies Sibirotitan as a relatively advanced non-titanosaurian somphospondyl.
The animal is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli and belongs to the larger group Saurischia.
It was found to share features of its vertebrae and ribs with Epachthosaurus and Euhelopus.

Sibirotitan lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 113 million years ago, specifically from the Barremian to the Aptian between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
The animal is considered one of the oldest known titanosauriform species found in Asia and was also noted as one of the oldest known sauropod species in the region.
